title: They'll Get It Elsewhere... If They Don't Get It From You
author: The Daily Dad
summary: This Daily Dad meditation begins from the premise that the need to be loved is a basic human need and arguably the root motivation of nearly everything people do. Quoting The Red Clay Strays' lyric 'I just wanna be loved', it argues that children who do not receive love from their parents will seek it elsewhere. The piece lists the substitutes: the attention of strangers, money or power, cults, toxic partners, drugs, or acting out. It places responsibility squarely on parents whose disapproval, reserve, or self-absorption creates the void, and warns against making conditional what should be unconditional. The meditation ends on reassurance and an instruction: most fathers do love their children, so they should make sure the children feel it and know they are worthy of it no matter what.
points: The need to be loved is framed as the root motivation behind nearly everything people do.
Children deprived of parental love seek validation from strangers, power, cults, toxic partners, drugs, or acting out.
Parental disapproval, reserve, and self-absorption are named as the sources of the void children try to fill.
Loving one's children is not enough; fathers must make that love felt and unconditional.
quotes: It’s a basic human need. It’s something that everyone wants, that everyone deserves. It is, you could argue, the root cause and motivation of nearly everything people do.
We want it. We need it. And when we don’t get it from our parents? Well, we try to get it from something or someone else.
From the attention of strangers, from money or power, from cults or toxic romantic partners, from drugs or acting out—your kids will find some way to feel validated or seen.
They will seek to fill the void that your disapproval, your reserve, your self-absorption created in them.
If you make conditional what should be unconditional, if you fail to love them—and to make them feel loved—they will find a way to get it from someone who will.
Let them feel it and understand that they are worthy of it, no matter what. That your love for them is unconditional and unlimited.
